newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso signs power production decree.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso signs power production decree.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has signed a decree laying down the regulatory terms for private power producers, Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito said.
The decree covers independent producers who sell their power to third-party consumers and auto-producers who generate energy for their own use but may also sell excess power, Brito said.
The minister said the decree was a important landmark in Brazil's program to encourage private investors to take over the state's role as producer and distributor of power.
The new rules guarantee access to Brazil's inter-regional transmission system and regional distribution networks for independent and auto-producers.

Seventy-four concessions have been awarded since January last year for the private construction and operation of hydro- and thermoelectric installations in Brazil, with a total capacity of 3,300 megawatts, Brito said.
A further 11 new hydroelectric projects, totalling 2,280 megawatts in capacity, were last week submitted for approval to the National Privatization Council.
Brito also announced forthcoming changes to power laws which require that any project over one megawatt be the subject of a public tender.
A bill currently in the Senate to set up the National Electric Energy Agency, a regulatory body, states that projects of up to 10 megawatts may be awarded via decree.
